ops.title: Exit-node degradation 2026-07: DERP relay is structural (double NAT + remote laptop), host machinery healthy
ops.body:
## Root cause

The laptop (yBook Pro) ↔ host (yasyf-home) WireGuard path cannot go direct, so **all exit-node traffic rides DERP**, and the laptop's current location makes that relay path cross-Pacific (~200ms). Two independent facts make direct impossible:

1. **Host is double-NATed.** Traceroute: host → eero `192.168.4.1` (LAN 192.168.4.0/22) → AT&T gateway `192.168.1.254` → public `104.1.90.148`. The eero's UPnP mapping (554 successes in daemon metrics) terminates at the eero's *private* WAN address `192.168.1.64` — the host advertises `192.168.1.64:64293`, which is internet-unreachable. STUN-derived `104.1.90.148:2969` is endpoint-dependent through two NAT layers. **No internet-reachable inbound UDP path to the host exists.**
2. **Laptop is currently in NZ** (clock UTC+12, public 27.123.145.42 = APNIC, DERP home syd at 47ms). Its UDP works (netcheck UDP:true, MappingVariesByDestIP:false) but no portmap protocol, and its carrier NAT filtering + the host's dead inbound = disco fails both directions (host saw 39 call-me-maybe batches, deleted all 58 candidate endpoints — none ever ponged).

## Measured quality classes (ephemeral probe on the host, 2026-07-15)

- Direct exit path (probe→host→NAT→WAN): egress `104.1.90.148`, DNS via socks5h OK, **54.9 MB/s (~440 Mbps ≈ 90% of the 61.1 MB/s baseline)** — host forwarding/NAT/DNS machinery is fully healthy.
- DERP-forced exit (`TS_DEBUG_ALWAYS_USE_DERP=1`, sfo relay at ~20ms): **2.78 MB/s (~22 Mbps), a 20× collapse** — and the laptop's relay RTT is 10× worse, so its ceiling is far lower → the observed slowness/stalls/DNS timeouts.

## What was ruled out

- disable-bind cap (7bef8e1): live and harmless — host→metal direct `via 192.168.64.11` (vmnet-direct works, 1-3ms).
- Host magicsock: rebind+restun run (counters 22 / 6862); no wedge.
- pf anchor, InternetSharing, forwarding sysctls, exit advertisement: all healthy.
- Host daemon = mise dev build 1.98.5-ERR-BuildInfo at /usr/local/bin/tailscaled (symlink since Jun 1 — not a recent change); plist last touched Jul 13 (`--port=41641`).

## Fixes (router/user level — host software cannot fix this)

- Best: **AT&T gateway IP passthrough to the eero** → eero WAN becomes 104.1.90.148 → its UPnP mapping becomes public → direct connections work (laptop would get ~130-160ms direct UDP instead of relayed TCP).
- Alternative: static double port-forward UDP 41641: AT&T → 192.168.1.64, eero → 192.168.4.24.
- en0 wired drop (unintended, still down — status: inactive, cable/link dead) is an independent quality issue; restore per Phase 4.
- IPv6 direct exists host-side (AT&T GUA advertised on :41641 — the probe connected via it) but the laptop's NZ network has no IPv6.

## Reusable probe harness (tested, answers "test exit node without the laptop")

Userspace tailscaled + SOCKS5 on the host itself; key minted via cookiesync → console API `POST login.tailscale.com/admin/api/public/tailnet/-/keys/` (untagged, ephemeral, preauthorized; `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin` + tailcontrol cookie). Pass A normal, Pass B with `TS_DEBUG_ALWAYS_USE_DERP=1`; `curl --proxy socks5h://localhost:1055` for exit-path DNS; cleanup = logout (ephemeral self-deletes) + kill + rm -rf /tmp/ts-probe.
